newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says wary about yen redenomination.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says wary about yen redenomination.

text.p: Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a parliamentary committee on Friday that Japan must be cautious about considering redenominating its currency.
"On redenomination, there's much cost involved here and this is likely to affect various areas. For now, it is an issue that would have to be considered cautiously," Matsushita said.
Matsushita had been asked by a parliament member about internationalisation of the yen.

Redenomination involves resetting the value of one unit of a currency. For example, the yen could be redenominated so that 100 yen became worth one yen, bringing it much closer in value to one dollar. One dollar is now worth about 116 yen.
Matsushita added that Japan's "Big Bang" financial reforms were meaningful and that he would like to cooperate in carrying them out.
